Q1: Copper(II) chloride exhibits known hazards across several categories, classified at Tier 1 for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), environmental impact (ENV), oral toxicity (ORL), and dermal/eye hazards (SKN). Additionally, it shows expanded evidence of endocrine disruption (EDC) and inhalation hazards (IHL) at Tier 2. Information regarding its organ and systemic hazards (OGN) is currently data deficient, indicating an unknown risk in this area.
Q2: Copper(II) chloride is identified on two significant "Lists of Concern." It appears on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and it is also included under the Clean Water Act, indicating its environmental relevance and regulatory oversight.
Q3: Copper(II) chloride is extensively characterized, evidenced by approximately 48,000 scientific literature references, which is significantly higher than the median for such compounds. Its specific molecular formula (Cl2Cu) and classification as a "Small Molecule" confirm it is a well-defined substance, with only one hazard category, Organ and Systemic hazards, currently lacking sufficient data.
